root_cause.text: AppArmor prematurely released the reference to `i_private` data (via `aa_put_ns`/`aa_put_proxy`/`aa_put_i_loaddata`) when removing file system dentries, while the inode could still be accessed by file operations after removal, resulting in a use-after-free race.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the reference release to the `evict_inode` callback (`aafs_evict`), removing manual `aa_put_*` calls in functions like `__aafs_profile_rmdir`, `__aafs_ns_rmdir`, and `remove_rawdata_dents`. For instance, in `__aafs_profile_rmdir` the old code had `aa_put_proxy(proxy);` after `aafs_remove`, and in `remove_rawdata_dents` there was `aa_put_i_loaddata(rawdata);` – these are removed and instead `aafs_evict` calls `aa_put_common_ref`. The CVE description explicitly states: "AppArmor was putting the reference to i_private data on its end after removing the original entry from the file system. However the inode can and does live beyond that point and it is possible that some of the fs call back functions will be invoked after the reference has been put, which results in a race." This confirms the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement releases the label reference inside free_proxy when the proxy refcount drops. If called prematurely during dentry removal while the inode still holds i_private, it frees the label leading to use-after-free.
This statement calls free_proxy inside aa_proxy_kref, which is invoked when the proxy reference count reaches zero. Premature release of the proxy during dentry removal causes use-after-free.

This function is the kref release handler for aa_proxy. It is called when the last reference to the proxy is dropped, triggering the free of i_private data. If called before file operations complete, it leaves a dangling pointer.
This structure defines the proxy that is stored as i_private in AppArmor inodes. The refcount field 'count' is mishandled during dentry removal, leading to premature free and use-after-free.

This structure provides the reference counting used by all AppArmor aafs data types. Release of references (via aa_put_ns/aa_put_proxy/aa_put_i_loaddata) during dentry removal while inodes remain accessible causes use-after-free.
